links.outcome: Detection latency and lead time before error onset
links.effect: Probe latency ~10ms per answer versus ~10s for multi-sample baselines; trigger fires roughly 10-35 tokens before error onset versus zero lead time for a post-hoc check
links.quote: Probe latency is ∼10ms per answer versus ∼10s for multi-sample baselines.

links.comparator_used: generation without probe-triggered intervention (implied unmitigated baseline)
links.outcome: Hallucination detection (EDR@5) and hallucination reduction under false-positive-rate caps
links.effect: EDR@5 up to 0.390 (PubMedQA) and 0.352 (MedHallu) at cap γ≤0.10, rising to 0.587 with 29%-59% hallucination reduction at cap γ≤0.20
links.tradeoff: Detection rate depends on the false-positive-rate cap, with lower EDR at the strict cap. The Endoscopy case study has wide confidence intervals because of a small confirmed-correct denominator (26-52 per backbone).
links.quote: On the public biomedical QA benchmarks the probe yields viable detection across all backbone-dataset combinations: EDR@5 up to 0.390 (PubMedQA) and 0.352 (MedHallu) at the strict cap γ≤0.10, rising to 0.587 with 29%-59% hallucination reduction at the monitoring cap γ≤0.20.

design_hint: real-time hallucination detection with FPR-constrained trigger calibration
